analysis_role: Post-result resolution sensitivity. Refit the already-frozen mutually adjusted BIO15/BIO1 + latitude/longitude Brownian models on the larger state-diverse panels already present in frozen occurrence assets. This tests whether the n=9 panel size alone explains failure of BIO15 axis specificity.

models.primary: Brownian GLS z(BIO15) ~ orientation + z(BIO1) + z(latitude) + z(longitude)
models.reciprocal: Brownian GLS z(BIO1) ~ orientation + z(BIO15) + z(latitude) + z(longitude)
models.robustness: species leave-one-out on every accepted topology
models.prediction: LOO Brownian conditional prediction of BIO15: BIO1 + latitude + longitude versus the same model plus orientation

decision_rule.specificity_recovered: n5 BIO15 orientation coefficient is positive on 6/6 topologies and all 72 n5 topology-by-species LOO fits; n3 is reported as a secondary boundary and cannot rescue failure at n5
decision_rule.direction_only: n5 BIO15 coefficient is positive on all six full fits but at least one n5 LOO fit reverses sign
decision_rule.direction_destabilized: at least one n5 full-topology BIO15 coefficient is non-positive
decision_rule.prediction_role: held-out MSE/MAE improvement is supporting only and cannot override the sign-based classification

claim_ceiling: The frozen n>=10 result remains primary; relaxed occurrence thresholds are sensitivity analyses only.
Lower occurrence counts increase centroid uncertainty and cannot create independent replication.
No new occurrence source, alias or environmental predictor is admitted.
No result establishes precipitation seasonality as a selective agent, historical cause, adaptation or plasticity.
Topology and leave-one-out stability are sensitivity diagnostics, not biological replicate counts.
